sections.html:
San Juan County's biggest city, Farmington, serves as the shopping and services center for the northwest corner of the state and the Four Corners. Three rivers come together here (the San Juan, Animas and La Plata) at 5,473 feet, and 46,624 people lived in town at the 2020 census. US 64 runs east and west through the city, and Four Corners Regional Airport offers flights. With that much water nearby, look at flood maps and insurance before you list.

The local economy has long moved with energy. Oil and gas investment arrived in the 1920s, the San Juan Basin natural gas pipeline followed in 1953, and the town felt price swings in the 1970s. Anyone who bought at the top of a boom and sells in a slump lives that history.

sections.h2: The San Juan Generating Station closure
sections.html:
The San Juan Generating Station closed in 2022, and the San Juan coal mine nearby closed with it. PNM, which led the ownership group, retired the final two units that year, the smokestacks came down in August 2024, and demolition and reclamation continue. The plant once generated 1,600 megawatts. The Four Corners Power Plant is slated for retirement in 2031.

Replacement spending exists but is slower than the loss. PNM is bonding up to $40 million under the 2019 Energy Transition Act for economic development, workforce retraining and severance in the region, and it is buying power from the San Juan Solar project, which includes 200 megawatts of solar and 100 megawatts of battery storage.

  • A major power plant and its mine are gone, and a second plant is due to retire in 2031.
  • Replacement money is tied to solar projects, retraining funds and economic development programs.
  • Lenders and buyers weigh job stability in the area.

When a layoff or a new job is pushing you to sell, a fast closing saves months of payments on a house that might otherwise linger unsold.

The climate is semi-arid, with a January daily low that averages 20 degrees and a July daily high near 90. Yearly precipitation is close to 8 inches, snowfall adds up to 8.6 inches, and the extremes have been minus 34 and 105 degrees.

Inspectors care about that cold-to-hot swing more than rainfall. Crawl space and exterior wall plumbing can freeze, roofs and decks bake in strong sun, and the furnace and the cooler both see heavy use.

A house close to the San Juan or Animas deserves a FEMA map lookup for its exact address, and a call to your insurer about coverage, before it goes on the market. County emergency management tracks river conditions. Lenders can require flood insurance in a mapped zone, which narrows the pool of buyers and slows some deals.

sections.h2: San Juan County property tax dates and penalties
sections.html:
Bills leave the county by November 1. Pay the whole amount or the first half by November 10; anything unpaid when business closes December 10 is delinquent. The second half comes due April 10 and goes delinquent after May 10.

Taxable value is one third of full value. Each September the state Department of Finance and Administration turns the budgets of the county, schools, cities and voter-approved bonds into a rate. A bill under $5 gets an administrative fee that brings it to $5. Paying late costs 1 percent interest plus a 1 percent penalty every month, with the penalty portion stopping at 5 percent.

A closing after that late August cutoff can leave the next bill in the seller's name. Talk to the title company about who covers what, and open any mail addressed to you after the sale.

sections.h2: What else changes the tax bill in a sale
sections.html:
On a sale by real estate contract, the bill keeps the earlier owner's name and adds the buyer's after "C/O" until the contract is paid off. A buyer with a recorded deed should visit the Assessor's office so the roll is right.

With escrow, the bill still comes to the owner, with a box checked to show the lender asked for it. An old escrow account can carry a wrong account number, so call the county at once if that box is checked and you have no lender. Never receiving a bill or notice of value does not cancel what you owe.

Before closing:

  • Find the newest bill and confirm both halves are paid.
  • Learn whether the buyer assumes escrow or pays cash.
  • Make sure the Assessor has your right mailing address.
  • Keep copies of every payment receipt.

A balance owed does not stop a sale. The tax, interest and penalty typically come out of your proceeds at the table. Phone the County Treasurer for today's figure before you say yes to an offer, then have the title company recheck it near signing. Charges keep growing monthly, so a house that is behind should move fast.

sections.h2: Which sale route fits in Farmington
sections.html:
Owners here have three paths: an agent listing, a direct sale to a buyer, or a cash sale to a company like ours. A listing can earn the best price for a house in good repair but brings showings, repair credits and a financing contingency. Direct sales help owners with inherited property, back taxes, tenants or deferred maintenance.

The city owns its electric utility, which serves roughly 46,000 metered customers across an area that extends past city limits. Someone comparing a city house with one just outside may find different utility arrangements, so be ready to explain yours.

We cannot promise a price, since offers reflect the property, its location and what it needs. Whatever you decide, see the terms in writing, learn who covers closing costs and who holds earnest money, and use a title company for the closing.

sections.h2: Practical steps for a quick sale
sections.html: Begin with money and paper: learn what you owe in tax and on any mortgage, and collect the deed and payment receipts. Then walk the house looking for the plumbing, roof and heating trouble that hard winters cause, and note what you find for disclosure. Decide if you can wait through a listing or need a set date, and choose accordingly. Last, contact a title company early so documents are ready when an offer arrives.

faqs.q: When are San Juan County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Mailing is by November 1. Pay in full or the first half by November 10; delinquency begins after December 10. Second-half payment is due April 10, delinquent after May 10.

faqs.q: Who pays property tax if I sell my Farmington house mid-year?
faqs.a: The statute names the January 1 owner, but buyer and seller commonly share the year at closing through the title company. Get the split in writing.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Farmington house with unpaid property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The balance, with interest and penalty, is normally taken from sale proceeds. The County Treasurer at (505) 334-9421 can give you today's amount.

faqs.q: Does the closing of the San Juan Generating Station make it harder to sell?
faqs.a: It reshaped local jobs, and some owners are selling after losing work. How it touches your sale depends on your neighborhood and the house's condition.

faqs.q: How do I check whether my Farmington house is in a flood zone?
faqs.a: Look up your address on the FEMA flood map and ask your insurer. Near the San Juan or Animas, do it before listing, because buyers' lenders may demand flood insurance.
